data.differential-against-gfortran-1520#Diffe:
foracle sema-rate --dir D parses and analyses every file and compares with gfortran -fsyntax-only, which also makes the semantic checks. The verdicts of gfortran are committed (sema/testdata/gf-*.tsv), so that sema/corpus_test.go asserts the counts without the compiler.
corpus files both accept refused only by us accepted only by us both refuse FCVS 180 179 0 1 0 gcc gfortran.fortran-torture 314 313 1 (parser) 0 0 gcc gfortran.dg 8 306 5 753 291 (125 parser, 166 analyser) 1 202 1 060 gfortran.dg, dg-do run files 3 151 2 675 155 95 226 The 1 202 files accepted only by us are the gfortran.dg tests written to be refused for reasons not checked yet (type-bound procedure rules, input/output tag checks, polymorphism, -std conformance). The refused-only-by-us files are defects or gaps of ours. BenchmarkAnalyze (the 12 programs of testdata/programs, one core) is 3 733 allocations and 550 KB per pass, exact; its time was not measured: load.
data.parse-rate-on-the-corpora#Parse rate on:
foracle parse-rate --dir D parses every Fortran file below D and runs gfortran -fsyntax-only on the same file. Numbers taken on the pinned revisions with gfortran 15.2.0:
corpus files we parse gfortran accepts both accept fail-only-ours fail-gfortran-only fail-both FCVS (fcvs21_f95) 180 180 (100 %) 179 179 0 1 0 gcc gfortran.fortran-torture 314 313 (99.7 %) 313 312 1 1 0 gcc gfortran.dg 8 306 7 496 (90.2 %) 6 096 5 973 123 1 523 687 Of the files gfortran accepts, the parser accepts 100 % of FCVS, 99.7 % of the torture suite and 98.0 % of gfortran.dg. The 123 gfortran.dg files that gfortran accepts and we refuse are, by first error: derived-type parameters (30, excluded from v1), DEC parameter x = v without parentheses and other extensions (28), preprocessor remnants of .F90 files (19), contains followed by module procedure (17, submodules are v1-excluded), coarray statements (7), files with more than 255 continuation lines (5, where gfortran is lenient and we apply the standard’s limit on purpose), Hollerith outside FORMAT, UTF-16/32 encodings, and a few single files.
Not measured yet: the throughput against gfortran -fsyntax-only. The development machine’s 1-minute load stayed between 10 and 100, above the fleet’s limit of 8, so parse-bench refused to run and no throughput figure is published rather than a loaded one. Allocation counts are exact under load: parsing the 19 testdata files is 4 470 allocations (380 KB) per pass.
data.semantic-analysis#Semantic analysis:
github.com/go-embedded-fortran/fortran/sema turns a parsed file into the typed tree: the syntax tree annotated by sema.Info (the design of go/types). Info.Types maps every expression to its type, kind, rank and constant value, Info.Uses maps a name to its symbol, Info.Scopes maps a program unit to its scope. Both back ends of bib section 4.2 walk the one tree. LFortran’s ASR is the design reference (BSD-3); no code was ported.
f, _ := syntax.Parse("a.f90", src, nil) info, errs := sema.Analyze(f, &sema.Options{ImplicitNone: true}) // errs: "a.f90:3:5: Symbol 'x' at (1) has no IMPLICIT type" Part 1: scopes and symbols, implicit typing and implicit none (Options.ImplicitNone is the notebook default), kinds validated against gfortran’s kinds, folding of named constants, typing of expressions with the promotion rules of Table 10.2, derived types, use association, iso_fortran_env and iso_c_binding constants, statement functions and statement checks. Part 2, calls: generic resolution (the typed tree names the specific), ambiguity (C1511, C1512, C1514), argument association (count, keywords, type, kind, rank, pointer/allocatable, definable intent(out) actuals), explicit-interface requirements, function versus subroutine, defined operations and assignment. Part 3, shapes: TV.Shape is the extent of each dimension, a number when it is a compile-time constant and -1 when it is not; conformance of operands, array assignments, initialisations, elemental arguments and where; the shape rules of reshape, matmul, transpose, dot_product, spread and the reductions. An unknown extent is never the reason for a refusal. The analyser never panics (a panic is recovered into an error and the fuzzer treats it as a failure); its bounds (Limits) are refusals, asserted by bomb tests.
data.the-cell-splitter-and-the-session-module:
sema.Session analyses the cells of a notebook in order, with the shape of go-notebook’s analysis.Sequential (Begin, AnalyzeNext(state, index, src)). syntax.Options.Cell is the grammar of a cell: statements outside any program unit are main-program material that needs no END. A cell is then split:
top-level declarations and top-level subroutines and functions go into the session module __cell; top-level executable statements are wrapped in the subroutine __cell_run, a procedure of that module; every earlier session module and every module an earlier cell defined is an implicit use of __cell; redefinition shadows; implicit typing is off unless SessionOptions.ImplicitTyping; a cell with errors returns the state it was given, so a broken cell leaves nothing behind. sema.GoType is the values table of bib section 7 (integer(k) to int8..int64, real to float32|float64, complex(4|8) to complex64|complex128, logical to bool, character to string, arrays to *ndarray.Array, derived types opaque; integer(16), real(10) and real(16) have none). The adapter that fills go-notebook’s analysis.Cell belongs to the language registration in go-notebook (analysis/parsers).
data.the-parser#The parser:
github.com/go-embedded-fortran/fortran/syntax is a pure-Go (CGO_ENABLED=0) lexer and recursive-descent parser producing a typed AST with byte offsets that resolve to file:line:col. The package documentation cites the clauses of F2018 (J3/18-007r1) that were read for it: 6.3.1 to 6.3.3 (source form, free and fixed), 6.4 (INCLUDE), and 10.1.1 (operator precedence). The AST design follows LFortran’s AST.asdl (BSD-3, a design reference); its GLR grammar is not ported.
f, err := syntax.Parse("prog.f90", src, &syntax.Options{FS: includeFS}) // err is a syntax.ErrorList: "prog.f90:12:7: expected ')', found ','" for _, u := range f.Units { ... } fmt.Print(syntax.Print(f)) // canonical free-form source; parses back to the same AST Source form by extension (.f .for .f77 .ftn fixed, the rest free, as gfortran) or Options.Form. INCLUDE resolves through Options.FS only: with a nil FS every include is refused, the host file system is never read by default, absolute and .. paths are refused, and an include of a file already being included is refused. Names and keywords are case-insensitive and normalised to lower case. There are no reserved words (if = 1 is an assignment). Errors are file:line:col: message; the parser recovers at the next statement and never panics. Bounds assert a refusal: source bytes (16 MiB, also summed over includes), nesting depth (200), include depth (8), continuation lines of a statement (255, the standard’s limit), tokens of a statement (262 144) and reported errors (50). Tests: a printer round trip on every file of testdata/programs and testdata/gate (19 files, all parse), golden AST dumps, three fuzz targets (FuzzParseFree, FuzzParseFixed, FuzzLex) whose corpus is committed, and bomb tests that assert a refusal under a soft memory limit.

data:
Package rt is the Fortran runtime’s formatted and list-directed input and output (bib section 5 row 1), in pure Go, ported from LLVM flang-rt (llvmorg-23.1.4, Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, see NOTICE and the headers of the ported files) and made to print what gfortran 15.2.0 prints, because that is what a notebook’s print * shows. eval’s print and write run on it (units *, 6 and 0; a format is a character literal or *).
tab := rt.NewTable(stdout, stderr, stdin, fsys) // units 6, 0, 5; fsys is read-only u := tab.Get(6) err := u.Write(rt.Spec{Format: "(F8.3,1X,ES12.4)", HasFormat: true}, []rt.Val{rt.Real8(3.14159), rt.Real8(1e-5)}) // nil, or *rt.Error{Stat, Msg} r := rt.NewInternalRead(" 12 3.5 abc") // read from a character variable err = r.Read(rt.Spec{}, items) // list-directed; items updated in place edit descriptors I B O Z F E D EN ES G L A; EX is implemented (flang-rt’s) but off, because gfortran 15.2 refuses it (rt.EnableEX) control X T TL TR / : kP S SP SS BN BZ RN RU RD RZ RC RP DC DP, quoted strings and nH, repeat counts, nested groups, *( ), format reversion list-directed output as gfortran; input with r*c, null values, /, quoted strings, complex pairs units in-memory table (5, 6, 0), read-only files on an fs.FS, in-memory scratch files with rewind/backspace, internal files (scalar and array), IOSTAT values as libgfortran’s, non-advancing output bounds format length, nesting depth, repeat count, field width, digits, items per statement, record length and file size are refusals, asserted under a memory limit; FuzzFormat and FuzzInput (corpus committed) Float to decimal is correctly rounded: TestDecimalAgainstBig compares the digits for the classic hard cases and 3000 random doubles, at 11 digit counts, with math/big; TestRoundingModesBracket checks RU, RD, RZ and RC against the exact expansion.
data.differential-against-gfortran-1520#Diffe:
rt/diff_test.go and rt/diffin_test.go generate programs (formats times values, including ±0, denormals, infinities, NaN, field overflow, huge widths, errors with iostat), compile and run them with the pinned gfortran, and compare the text byte for byte with rt’s. Last run, 71 135 cases: 71 096 identical, 39 differing in documented classes, 0 unexplained.
area cases identical kept differences REAL(8) and REAL(4), every real edit descriptor, widths, digits, kP, S, rounding modes, DC 63 674 63 648 26: EN with many digits (REAL(4) with d ≥ 6 at a carry boundary, d ≥ 16): gfortran rounds to d+1 digits and pads with zeros INTEGER, LOGICAL, CHARACTER, B/O/Z, mismatches 4 063 4 063 control edit descriptors, reversion, T/TL/TR, format errors 86 86 list-directed output (REAL, COMPLEX, mixed lists, 40-item lines) 632 632 formatted and list-directed input 2 576 2 563 13: BZ with an exponent letter or a lone sign (6), ; without DC (1), a cut-short complex (6) repeat counts r*c 104 104 The differences gfortran has from the standard (and from flang-rt) that rt copies are listed in the package documentation (go doc ./rt): F0.d prints .50, E0.d an E+000 exponent, G8.1 of 0.95 is 1., I5.8 is refused, A and L accept integers, a repeat count cannot cross kinds on input, and so on. Of the 14 golden programs, eval runs all 14 and they are byte-identical to their goldens (stdout, stderr, exit status); TestGoldenPrograms counts the runs and the refusals.
data.performance#Performance: A statement on a warm unit allocates nothing (0 allocations for F, ES and list-directed writes, asserted by TestAllocations; formats are compiled once and cached). Throughput against gfortran’s own I/O is RT_PERF=1 go test ./rt -run TestPerfVsGfortran -v (interleaved rounds, single core, gfortran -O2); it refuses to measure at a one-minute load of 8 or more. Not measured: load (the machine was at 38 to 51 when this was written); no figure is claimed.

data.the-gate-bib-section-42#The gate (bib se:
foracle gate decides between (A) a pure-Go evaluator and (B) compiling to wasm32. The decision rule is fixed in bib section 4.2 and implemented once, in internal/gate/rule.go, with its thresholds (5, 2, 1.2) pinned by a test.
contender what it is A package eval (prototype, the seed of M3-A): the typed tree compiled once into closures over typed slots; real(8) arrays of rank 1 and 2, column-major, bounds-checked; whole-array expressions and matmul handed to go-ndarray v0.40.3 B-near, B-upper the C transliterations in testdata/gate/c/ compiled by clang 23.1.4 to wasm32-wasip1 at -O0 and -O2, run on wazero v1.12.0 (the version go-embedded-c pins) gfortran 15.2.0 -O2, native: the reference direct go-ndarray called straight from Go, no evaluator, no copy: the baseline of A’s array kernels Every contender times its kernel with a clock around the kernel itself, one core (GOMAXPROCS=1), in interleaved rounds (7 rounds, median and spread). A checksum out of its bound is a failure, not a time. The bound is computed with math/big and a contender is within 1.01 * m * 2^-53 * exact, m being the number of rounding steps on the longest chain of the kernel (nonnegative data, so the bound holds for any summation order, FMA or vectorisation).
Only the desktop home is implemented: the playground (headless Chromium) needs a browser lane that does not exist yet (#5). The rule needs both homes to pick A, so with the desktop alone it can only answer B or “A first”.
data.the-oracle#The oracle:
The reference is gfortran 15.2.0 run natively (GCC releases/gcc-15.2.0): it is the compiler LFortran’s and llvm-test-suite’s reference outputs are made with. It is GPL and is only ever run as a program, never linked or ported (see NOTICE). “Correct” means the same exit status and the same stdout and stderr bytes, except where the output is processor-dependent (bib section 8).
go install github.com/go-embedded-fortran/fortran/cmd/foracle@latest export FORACLE_HOME=$HOME/foracle-home foracle toolchain # installs gfortran 15.2.0 into $FORACLE_HOME, no root foracle version foracle run prog.f90 # compile with the oracle, run, relay stdout/stderr/status gfortran is obtained as the conda-forge package gfortran==15.2.0, installed by a pinned micromamba (release 2.10.0-0, sha256 checked) into $FORACLE_HOME/env. foracle checks gfortran --version and refuses anything but 15.2.0. macOS arm64 and Linux amd64 are supported. flang 23.1.4 is optional and Linux only; that path is written but not exercised by CI yet.
Programs are compiled with -O0 -w -fno-backtrace. Runs are bounded: a wall-clock timeout (10 s), a cap on stdout and stderr (1 MiB), a fixed environment and an address-space limit (1 GiB). The memory limit is enforced on Linux; macOS accepts RLIMIT_AS but does not enforce it.
command what it does foracle golden regenerates testdata/programs.golden from the 14 programs in testdata/programs/ foracle corpus --dir D compiles and runs every Fortran file below D; one line per file foracle bench the reference column of the gate: the four kernels with gfortran -O2, 7 rounds, median and spread; refuses above 1-minute load 8 foracle gate [--smoke] [--wait-load D] the whole gate: the contenders on the kernels, checksum bounds, the decision rule; refuses above 1-minute load 8, or with --wait-load waits and reruns a round the load spoiled foracle parse-rate --dir D parses every Fortran file below D and compares with gfortran -fsyntax-only foracle parse-bench --dir D parse throughput against gfortran -fsyntax-only; refused above load 8 foracle toolchain --home H [--flang] installs the pinned toolchain foracle version prints the pinned versions and whether the toolchain was found The 14 golden programs (testdata/programs/*.f90) are original: list-directed and formatted output, integer and real kinds, arrays and sections, column-major order, modules, derived types, recursion, strings and internal I/O, stop, error stop and stderr. CI regenerates the golden file on linux/amd64 and darwin/arm64 and requires no difference.
No corpus is committed (the gcc testsuite is GPL; FCVS has its own terms). CI fetches them by commit: gcc gfortran.dg and gfortran.fortran-torture (gcc 15.2.0, 5115c7e447fc), llvm-test-suite FCVS (19b349c5aa39) and LFortran integration_tests (4f2cd049c87f).

data.not-yet#Not yet: Semantics not done, of bib section 1.1: shapes of pointer assignment, of forall and of type-bound results, type-bound generics and pass, the !GCC$ ATTRIBUTES NO_ARG_CHECK directive, select type dispatch, derived-type I/O, submodules, entry result typing, common/equivalence storage rules, data value conversion, and the “value from Go into a cell” direction of bib section 7. Not parsed yet: submodule procedure bodies, derived-type parameters (refused by design), coarray and team statements, do concurrent locality specifiers, Hollerith constants outside FORMAT, Cray pointers and DEC extensions, and # preprocessor directives (such lines are skipped, never interpreted). The flang path of the oracle is not exercised in CI, and the Linux memory limit is tested only in CI.
data.running-cells-m5-v0170#Running cells (M5:
eval.Session is sema.Session plus the evaluator: Run(ctx, src, out, stderr) analyses, compiles and runs one cell. What a cell defines stays for the cells after it: its variables keep their values (they are variables of the session module __cell, whose frame lives as long as the session), its modules, types, subroutines and functions are in scope, and a redefinition shadows. A program unit in a cell runs after the cell’s loose statements.
Output is per cell: standard output to out, standard error and the text of STOP to stderr; STOP and ERROR STOP end the cell, not the session. A cell the analyser or the compiler refuses is an *Error with a cellN.f90:line:col position and leaves the session as it was. A cell that fails while it runs keeps what it had done. Untrusted input: every DO iteration and procedure call is one step against SessionOptions.MaxSteps (default 2^32) and the context is looked at every 2^16 steps, so an infinite loop or an exponential recursion ends with step limit reached or the context’s error; the count, not a timer, is what holds in WebAssembly. MaxArrayElems, MaxStringLen and MaxCallDepth apply per run. Session.Get(name) reads a scalar variable of the session as a Go value. Arrays and derived types are not read yet; nothing crosses to other languages yet (go-notebook’s Fortran cells are Isolated, as R’s). Host and module association of arrays and of the DO variable now works. An array declared with an initialisation, which used to be dropped silently, is refused until it is implemented. CellInfo.Uses includes the derived types a cell’s declarations name and the modules its use statements name, not only the names in expressions. Resource bounds are refusals: an array of more than MaxArrayElems (2^28) elements, a character result of more than MaxStringLen (2^26) characters and an output list of more than MaxArrayElems values are refused at run time before anything is allocated.
